topics.topic: Required handling and invariant coverage for SQLite database or journal symlinks introduced after startup
questions: If the database or journal path is replaced by a symlink after the start walk but before SQLite opens it, must the call refuse with nothing written, or are SQLite-managed files exceptions to the later-symlink rule and the formal invariant `symlink_inside(data_directory) -> refused`?

Does the later-link refusal apply to SQLite-managed database and journal paths, and if so, how is it guaranteed across the race between the start walk and SQLite's open when SQLite cannot use `O_NOFOLLOW`?
Is the formal invariant intended to cover a database or journal symlink introduced after startup, or must it be narrowed to paths opened by the store itself and links present during the startup walk?
What must happen if the database or journal pathname is replaced by a symbolic link after the startup walk or between that walk and SQLite's open, and what enforces that result?

quotes:
The database file and its journal are
opened by SQLite, which Python cannot ask to refuse a link: the start's walk
finds no link before the database is opened, and afterwards only the
kernel's user can place one, the directory being private.

A link
found at start stops the start, and one found later makes that store call
fail with nothing written.
judgement.why: SQLite cannot be instructed to refuse a database or journal symlink introduced after the walk, while the later-link rule and formal invariant require every such link to be refused.

topics.topic: SQLite journal mode, auxiliary-file set, and scope of the SQLite-managed-file exception
questions: Which SQLite-created files are covered by “its journal”—a rollback journal, WAL and shared-memory files, temporary databases, or every auxiliary file SQLite may create—and do all receive the stated exception?
Which SQLite-created or opened files are covered by this exception: only the main database and rollback journal, or also WAL, shared-memory, statement-journal, temporary and other auxiliary files?
Which SQLite journal mode and associated file layout must the store use?
Which SQLite-opened files are exempt from the store's `O_NOFOLLOW` rule, and which SQLite journal mode and auxiliary-file set may the implementation use?

quotes:
The database file and its journal are
opened by SQLite, which Python cannot ask to refuse a link: the start's walk
finds no link before the database is opened, and afterwards only the
kernel's user can place one, the directory being private.

record_change: [PATH_OR_ARTIFACT_POLICY] Durability order: every file a change names is published, fsynced and its directory fsynced before the change is committed, and the SQLite database runs with synchronous FULL, so after a power loss a committed record never names a missing or partial file; a file published by a change that then failed stays unnamed: a value file until the next start removes it, a spooled file until it is replaced at its position or its run's spool is removed (A18 rule 4).

open_store: [BEHAVIOR] MUST run, in this order, stopping at the first failure: take an exclusive non-blocking lock on data_directory itself, opened as a directory without following links and held for the life of the process, so the lock creates no file; check that data_directory and everything inside it are owned by the process's effective user and grant no permission to group or others; walk the directory without following links and find no symbolic link; then open the database file inside data_directory as the module's one SQLite connection with synchronous FULL, after os.lstat finds that path no symbolic link; create its tables with create_store_schema, which leaves existing tables as they are; then remove the module's own temporary files left by an interrupted publish and every file of the content-addressed area whose digest no StoredValue names — a trial case's file fixture is itself a StoredValue of file carriage (M21), so no other record names a value file —, which is a digest for which list_stored_value_rows_by_value_digest answers no row, and create the content-addressed area and the spool area when absent.
judgement.divergence: One implementer can use rollback-journal mode and treat only the main database and rollback journal as SQLite-managed exceptions; another can use WAL mode and exempt the database, WAL and shared-memory files, which the owner operating or inspecting the data directory notices through different files and recovery or locking behaviour.
judgement.why: Neither State 2 nor the later texts choose a journal mode or define which SQLite auxiliary files are included by “its journal,” despite making that set an exception to the no-follow policy.

topics.topic: Definition and enforcement of the Linux-only host restriction under compatibility or virtualization
questions: What enforces the Linux-only rule if a non-Linux host or compatibility environment can make the sandbox probe succeed, and what definition of “host” determines whether that environment is allowed?

What determines that a host is non-Linux when a compatibility or virtualization layer can successfully execute the pinned bubblewrap probe, and what enforces the claim that every non-Linux host necessarily fails it?

quotes:
A release runs on Linux and on
no other host (owner, 2026-10-18). The kernel does not test the host: on any
other the sandbox probe of the start sequence (A03) fails and the start
stops, and any Linux on which that probe passes is a host; no version is
named.
judgement.why: The text explicitly defines an accepted host as Linux where the sandbox probe passes, assigns no separate host test, and asserts that the probe stops startup elsewhere.

topics.topic: Protection against symlinks inserted into ancestor components of store-managed paths after startup
questions: How does a store call detect and refuse a symlink inserted into an ancestor directory after start, given that `O_NOFOLLOW` on the final file open does not prevent following symlinked path components?

Must every store path be traversed through already-open directory descriptors so that a link introduced in an intermediate component makes the call fail, or is only the final pathname component protected?

quotes:
Every
file of the directory the store opens itself is opened without following
symbolic links, with Linux's `O_NOFOLLOW` on every open, never first asking
whether the flag exists (A20 rule 3).

A link
found at start stops the start, and one found later makes that store call
fail with nothing written.

record_change: [PATH_OR_ARTIFACT_POLICY] Every file and directory the module itself opens under the data directory MUST be opened without following symbolic links, by os.O_NOFOLLOW on each open; the host is Linux (A18), so no code checks that the flag exists; the database file and its journal, which sqlite3 opens and cannot be told to refuse a link, are covered by open_store's walk before the connection opens and by the directory's privacy after; a symbolic link met by any call after start makes that call raise StoreInternalError with nothing written.
judgement.divergence: One implementer traverses every component relative to already-open directory descriptors and refuses an ancestor replaced by a symlink; another reopens a full pathname and applies `O_NOFOLLOW` only to each final open, allowing an ancestor replacement to redirect the operation, which the owner notices as an escaped write or failure to enforce the store boundary.
judgement.why: The texts require no-follow opens and refusal of later links but never specify race-safe directory-relative traversal for store-managed paths.

topics.topic: Secure traversal flags for configuration and credential path components, including execute-only directories
questions: Which flags and directory-relative mechanism are used for intermediate components, and must an execute-only but unreadable directory component be accepted or refused?
Exactly how are path components opened, and which otherwise valid paths are refused because a directory component cannot be opened with the chosen flags?

quotes:
Here and in rule 2 the path is opened component by component without
following a symbolic link at any of them, each component with Linux's
`O_NOFOLLOW` — the host is Linux (A20 rule 3), so no code asks whether the
flag exists and there is no mode without it —, and the checks and the read
use that one opened file, so the file checked is the file read.

A credential is resolved only when a request to its service is built: its
secret file is read then, without following a symbolic link, and must be a
regular file owned by the kernel's user with no permission for group or
others; its content decoded as UTF-8, without one trailing newline, is the
value.

read_configuration: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise InstallationRejectedError naming the first failing check, in this order: config_path cannot be opened component by component without following a symbolic link at any component, every component opened with os.O_NOFOLLOW, which the Linux host always has (A17), so its presence is never tested, the file so opened is not a regular file, is not owned by the process's effective user, or grants any permission to group or others; the bytes cannot be read or do not parse as one JSON object whose members are exactly the fields of Installation with their types; a service appears twice in service_instances or in service_credentials; a credential header name is not an HTTP field-name token (one or more of the token characters of RFC 9110: letters, digits and the symbols allowed there); a credential's secret_file is not an absolute path; the owner token or any agent token is shorter than the imported ACCESS_TOKEN_LENGTH_MIN constant; two tokens among the owner token and the agent tokens are equal; two agent tokens have the same name. The ownership, mode and regular-file checks and the read MUST all use that one opened file, so the file checked is the file read.

resolve_service_credential: [BEHAVIOR] MUST find the service_credentials entry of service_id and read, at this call and never earlier, the file at its secret_file path, opened component by component without following a symbolic link at any component, each with os.O_NOFOLLOW used unconditionally (A17), the checks and the read using that one opened file, which must be a regular file, owned by the process's effective user and granting no permission to group or others; the value is the file's content decoded as UTF-8 with exactly one trailing newline removed when present.
judgement.divergence: One implementer opens intermediate directories with a directory-capable path-only descriptor and accepts execute-only directories; another uses read-only directory descriptors and refuses the same otherwise traversable configuration or credential path, which the owner notices at startup or when a service request fails with `credential_unresolved`.
judgement.why: The texts mandate component-wise `O_NOFOLLOW` but leave the directory-relative mechanism and intermediate-component open flags unspecified, making the exact refusal conditions implementation-dependent.

topics.topic: Startup-check precedence between the sandbox probe and Linux-only file-opening features on unsupported hosts
questions: Must the sandbox probe run before any A17 or A18 use of Linux-only `O_NOFOLLOW`, or may an unsupported host stop earlier because that flag or its semantics are unavailable?
On a non-Linux host, must startup reach and fail the sandbox probe specifically, or may loading or using `O_NOFOLLOW` fail first; and which startup check has precedence?

quotes: run_start_sequence: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST call, in exactly this order and each exactly once: load_installation with config_path; check_installed_instances with the loaded Installation; open_store with that Installation's data_directory; probe_sandbox; recover_in_flight_attempts; recover_running_runs (A03 rule 8, A09 rule 1, A14 rule 5, A18).

run_start_sequence: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Every step is required: the first step that raises — InstallationRejectedError, RefusedError from the instance check, a store refusal, SandboxUnavailableError, StopRequiredError or any other exception — stops the sequence there and propagates unchanged to the caller, the same exception with its own reason; before it propagates MUST write the failing step's name — load_installation, check_installed_instances, open_store, probe_sandbox, recover_in_flight_attempts or recover_running_runs — as one line to standard error, so the step is named there and the reason stays the exception's own; no later step runs and nothing is retried or skipped.
judgement.why: The later orchestration text fixes installation and store checks before the sandbox probe and says the first raised failure stops startup, so an unsupported host may fail during an earlier platform-specific file operation.

topics.topic: Handling of empty, dot, and dot-dot components in configuration and secret-file paths
questions: How are empty, `.` and `..` components in the absolute configuration or secret-file path handled: traversed literally, normalized, or refused?

topics.topic: Whether accepted Linux hosts must use the exact pinned sandbox runtime version
questions: May a Linux host whose installed sandbox runtime has a different version run the release when its probe passes, or must the exact pinned runtime version also be established?
